title: Kestrel Pay — opportunity scratchpad
content:
Quick context / why this matters:
- Kestrel Pay is a mid-market payments processor focused on marketplaces and platform businesses (confirmed via press release Oct 2024). They do 100–500M ARR (estimate), several multi-sided clients, expanding fraud/merchant risk product line.
- Their team repeatedly calls out the need for low-latency, high-throughput inference for real-time risk scoring and chat-based merchant support (see keynote clip in folder).
- We can uniquely pitch: predictable latency at scale, private deployment option for regulated partners, and cost controls via Redwood Optimize.

Top hypotheses to validate in discovery:
1) Primary pain is inference latency causing timeouts in fraud pipeline OR high per-call cost for batch scoring.
2) They care about model explainability for regulators and dispute cases.
3) They will require an offline auditing copy of inference logs (retention controls, redaction).
4) Pricing sensitivity vs. building self-hosted vs. using our Hosted API with Reserved/Dedicated options.

Key contacts / roles (to map outreach):
- Head of Platform: Alessandra Ruiz (likely technical buyer)
- Dir. of Risk Ops: Marco Alvarez (user of scoring/rules)
- Eng Manager, ML Infra: Priya Gupta (involved with deployment choices)
- Head of Commercial/Partnerships: Ben Troy (economic decision)

Upfront value props to test in outreach:
- "Cut decision latency in fraud flows by 30–60% while reducing per-call cost via smart batching & caching."
- "Private deployment option with KMS + audit logs to keep merchant data in your VPC."
- "Seamless fallback to smaller quantized model variants when capacity is constrained — avoids cascades of errors."

Email cold outreach templates (short, for A/B):
A (technical hook):
Subject: 30% faster scoring during peak for Kestrel Pay?
Hi Alessandra — quick note: we help payments platforms move real-time risk scoring off the critical path without breaking latency SLOs. We do this with a GPU-optimized serving runtime, prefix caching, and tiered fallbacks so your disputes/risk queues don't stall during spikes. Any interest in a 20–30 min sync to see a latency profile tailored to Kestrel?
— Jordan

B (commercial + compliance hook):
Subject: Private inference + audit logs for marketplace risk
Ben — Redwood has a private deployment path (VPC + KMS) that some processors use to meet audit requirements while reducing unit inference cost vs. in-house. Can I share a short one-pager showing numbers for a 200M ARR payments stack?

Call script bullets (discovery-first):
- One-sentence value: "We run LLM inference reliably at production scale for payments — low latency, predictable cost, and isolation options."
- Ask: "Walk me through a recent incident where risk scoring slowed or costs spiked — what happened?"
- Technical: "What models are you currently using? TF/PyTorch? Self-hosted endpoints?"
- Compliance: "Any required retention window for inference logs? Do you need full request traces or redacted outputs only?"
- Success criteria: "What would a successful pilot look like in 30–60 days?"

Objections playbook (short bullets):
- "We already self-host and own infra" -> pivot: "Great — many teams self-hosted and still adopt Redwood Private to avoid operational drift and get better kernel/quantization work we already do (saves 20–40% on unit cost). We can run a migration test in a staging VPC with no data egress."
- "Data & compliance concerns" -> pivot: "Private deployment, customer-managed KMS, and in-flight redaction. Also we offer fine-grained audit logs and retention controls to meet SOC/PCI-like needs."
- "Costs more than in-house" -> pivot: "We can show TCO for a 24/7 scoring pipeline including SRE and model ops — our Optimize recommendations typically reduce token cost and increase throughput, frequently offsetting fees for medium-sized processors."

Integration notes (tech bullets for discovery):
- Typical integration pattern: upstream queue -> enrichment -> call to Redwood inference endpoint (sync) -> result to rules engine -> scoring decision.
- Preferred latency target: p95 < 120ms for single-turn scoring (need to confirm).
- If they require per-merchant model variants, discuss multi-tenant routing and model pinning per customer ID.
- Data footprint: expect 1–5KB per request (mostly transaction metadata + encoded features).

Pilot proposal outline (for later):
- 4-week pilot: staging deployment (Hosted or Private), 2 test cases: 1) synthetic spike load to validate p95 latency; 2) live shadow run on 5% traffic to compare scoring parity and cost.
- Deliverables: latency/cost dashboard, failure-mode runbook, decision tree for rollout (canary thresholds).
- Success metrics: p95 latency improvement >=25% or cost per 1M calls reduced >=20% without regression in scoring precision.

Competitive landscape notes (quick):
- They may have looked at cloud vendors' managed endpoints (GCP/Azure) — advantage vs cloud: tuned serving runtime and automatic batching for diverse sequence lengths, better unit economics for high QPS workloads.
- Other LLM platforms: likely similar feature set, but we emphasize private deploy + explicit rollback/fallback routing policies.

Open research items / things to confirm in first call:
- exact current throughput (TPS) and peak QPS numbers; monthly inference volume; token sizes; typical request size (bytes)
- what models they currently prefer (LLMs for scoring? ensemble of models + heuristics?)
- SLA expectations (uptime, p95/p99) and whether they have fallback plan today
- legal: specific contract/attestation needs (PCI? SOC2? ISO?).

Next actions (this week):
- Send A and B emails to Alessandra and Ben (Maya to CC for intro).
- Prep a one-pager showing cost comparison for 50k, 250k, 1M calls/day (use Redwood Optimize baseline). Liam to run quick calc (see linked PR).
- Draft tailored pilot statement for Kestrel (include audit log retention options).
- Add a short demo script with a simulated scoring flow (sample dataset could be anonymized dataset from payments-demo repo).

Notes to self (rambling):
- Might be good to call out specific fraud/scoring use cases where interpretability matters (chargeback disputes, AML flags). If they use explainers, note Redwood's structured output support (function-calls/structured JSON) for downstream systems.
- If they push back on migration time, propose a shadow-run first with no user-facing impact.
- Keep outreach short; platform buyers respond better to 1–2 sentence propositions + a single CTA (time or paper).

Last thought: watch for signals in their job posts (ML infra hires) — new hiring suggests willingness to reconsider infra spend and potential for more aggressive pilots.

-- End scratchpad --
